_comment: The field DocOga plays on — verified by web research on 2 Nov 2026, re-verified 4 and 7 Nov 2026 (docs/COMPETITOR_WATCH.md). tools/competitor_watch.py reads the public feeds here every Monday (₦0: RSS, sitemaps, YouTube channel feeds; nothing that needs a login) and hands the brain what the field published, so every DocOga post is written knowing what the others said — to say it better, cite the section they did not, and take the angle they missed. Never to copy. Add a competitor only with a source you read; never a guess.

competitors.name: NigeriaBuildingCost — tenancy agreement generator
competitors.note: Free generator, 36 states + FCT, printed copy watermarked; ₦4,000 one-time pass removes the watermark for 90 days ("all 6 tools": BOQ, quotation, invoice, estimator, tenancy agreement, BOQ import) and a ₦500 seven-day pass on the pricing page; agency 10% / legal 10% written into the default agreement; notice-to-quit clause is a generic 1 week/1 month/1 quarter/6 months list that says "confirm the statutory requirement"; sample library (30 Oct) behind a free account. Re-read 7 Nov 2026: unchanged. Its sitemap dates public construction tenders daily — watched with /construction-tenders/ excluded.

competitors.name: Wonder.Legal Nigeria
competitors.note: Questionnaire templates (Word + PDF) incl. a free basic rent receipt (rev. 9 Aug 2026) and about twenty housing letters — notice to quit, late rent notice, lease renewal, and a **Change of Rent Notice** (rev. 18 Aug 2026) that is generic for all states, names the Lagos excluded areas, and tells the tenant who disagrees to "be ready to vacate" (no s.37, no notice ladder). Re-read 7 Nov 2026.

competitors.name: DIYLaw
competitors.note: Paid per document, Nigeria-drafted: tenancy agreement ₦3,500, employee contract ₦3,500, NDA ₦5,000, privacy policy ₦2,000; board resolution and letter of confirmation free; VAT added. Site banner (7 Nov 2026) says CAC/FIRS delays are slowing its registrations business.

competitors.name: SabiLaw Solutions
competitors.note: Lawyer-prepared Word templates, ₦3,200 each, one-time purchase, instant download: tenancy agreement, 6-month tenancy agreement, 7 days' owner's intention to recover possession, demand letter for payment of debt. Re-read 7 Nov 2026: unchanged, product pages dated Dec 2022.

competitors.name: Legalnaija templates
competitors.note: Short questionnaire → paid download at app.legalnaija.com/shop/templates (the explainer post is from Mar 2022); also a legal-information blog with steady but general posts (colloquia, arbitration). Re-read 7 Nov 2026: unchanged.

competitors.name: Rently.ng
competitors.note: Landlord SaaS: free plan (1 property, 3 tenants) with payment ledger + one-click PDF receipts, tenant portal links and "legal notices — quit notices, breach notices, rent demand letters in seconds" marked Free; agreement generator + e-sign, reminders (email/WhatsApp/SMS) and reports on Premium ₦5,000/month (₦50,000/year); Enterprise ₦15,000/month (₦170,000/year); tenant verification from ₦10,000. Claims 5,000+ landlords. Re-read 7 Nov 2026.

competitors.name: Homz.ng
competitors.note: Listings marketplace first (rent / buy / shortlet / land, Lagos-heavy) with property-management tools behind sign-in that generate agreements, quit notices and receipts; subscription. Re-read 7 Nov 2026: home page is listings only; no public document pages to watch.

competitors.name: Mushrooms.ng blog
competitors.note: The strongest content rival, and since 20 Oct 2026 a tool rival too: its "rent increase letter" post is a two-sided generator ("I'm raising the rent / My rent went up") with city-level rent comparison for 16 cities, a tenant's reply, PDF/WhatsApp/image output and blank Word/PDF templates — free, no sign-up — plus four copy-and-fill letters; the sample carries invented names. 5 Nov 2026: "How much can a landlord increase rent in Nigeria" (no legal percentage; Lagos s.37 + s.37(4); the 20% House motion of Oct 2025 is not law; excluded areas; s.4 advance rent; "other states: check your state's law" — no Enugu cap, no section outside Lagos) and "7 days notice to quit"; 20–22 Oct burst of about fifteen tenancy-law explainers; moving-out checklists 2 Nov. Cites Nairametrics 50–100% increase reports as fact. No RSS (/feed/ 404) — watched through the sitemap, /blog/ paths only.

competitors.name: Lexpraxis Solicitors blog
competitors.note: Corporate/business law firm (company formation, tax, IP, data protection; a real-estate transactions service page added Sep 2026); tenancy explainers are occasional (the Tenancy Bill 2025 clause by clause, Aug 2026). Re-read 7 Nov 2026: no new tenancy post.

competitors.name: Olamide Oyetayo Legal
competitors.note: Abuja/Lagos firm; landlord-side eviction explainers (Recovery of Premises Act, Lagos Tenancy Law) and, in 2026, buyer-side Abuja property checks; insights feed is WhatsApp-CTA driven. Re-read 7 Nov 2026: latest insights are property purchase and business contracts, not tenancy.

competitors.name: AALAWSNG — Adeola Kolawole (YouTube)
competitors.note: Aviel Avenante Law Practice's channel (id read from its own Posts tab, 4 Nov 2026). Law-talk videos, lawyer-to-camera; the one tenancy explainer ('Nigerian Tenancy Law: Notice to Quit', Nov 2022, 1,625 views) is old — 2026 output is wills, medical consent, company law, land titles. Low priority; the Atom feed answered 404 on the 4 Nov pull though the id is the channel's own, so the source line may read 'unreachable' until YouTube serves it.

competitors.name: @legalfriendng — Real Estate Lawyer (TikTok)
competitors.note: Reacts to viral tenant stories with the Lagos Tenancy Law section (ss.6–7 on improvements, Oct 2026). TikTok has no public feed at ₦0 — watched by hand, not by the machine.

competitors.name: @talk360law — KING, ESQ. (TikTok)
competitors.note: Benin-based lawyer; 'lawyer reacts' format on tenant stories (788 likes / 183 comments on one, Oct 2026). No public feed at ₦0.

competitors.name: @theonlybusayoadesanya (TikTok)
competitors.note: Lawyer; quit-notice timing videos picked up by Legit.ng (Sep 2025). No public feed at ₦0.
